# Capability slices: every capability the mockup demonstrates, its slice and its plan

Lane RECONCILE-CAPABILITY, design-system pass, 27 September 2026. Ticket "Reconcile the fresh audit with the placeholder register" (#326) on the map "Ops Astro design system" (#287). It answers to `DIRECTION.md`, points 6 and 7: what a control does in the mockup demonstrates a capability Ops Astro must really have; the roadmap decides how it works; where the roadmap is silent, the obvious behaviour is decided and recorded. The owner, on #326: every capability slots into its existing slice, and **no doubling up**: a capability already planned gets a pointer to its slice and ticket, never a new one. Plan and document only.

## How to read this file

- **Source.** The placeholder register, `PLACEHOLDERS.md` (640 controls after this pass), is the one register of controls and their tracked actions. This file groups those controls into capabilities and places each in its slice. It is not a second register: the control rows, their looks and their full wording stay in `PLACEHOLDERS.md`.
- **One row per capability.** Controls are grouped when they share a ticket and a tracked action (every control that writes `task.due changed` through the dock task panel is one capability), or when they share a ticket and only navigate or change a per-person view. A register candidate always stands alone.
- **Slice** is a slice of the mockup-parity ticket plan (`docs/mockup-inventory/TICKET-PLAN.md`), with the roadmap phase that supplies its data and authority (`evidence/SLICE-INVENTORY.md` section 2.1). Section 15 holds capabilities that belong to a roadmap phase with no ticket-plan slice.
- **Planned by** names the ticket that already carries the capability: its `MP-x-y` ticket first, then any other ticket-plan, product (`ops-astro#n`) or roadmap (`roadmap#n`) ticket its register rows cite. **new candidate Cn** means nothing plans it yet: `Cn` is the proposed ticket in the register's candidate list (`PLACEHOLDERS.md`, "Candidate tickets for the build map"). Each candidate was checked against `evidence/SLICE-INVENTORY.md` (sections 1, 3 and 5) before it was kept.
- **Tracked action** is the record or event the capability writes, and whether it is audited (appended to the business's audit chain). `none` rows navigate or change only the reader's view; per-person preferences are saved and not audited (`docs/decisions/delivery-and-presence.md:25`).
- **Fresh** lists the rows of the capability-first fresh audit (`evidence/fresh-audit/`) that confirm the capability. **Authority** lists the decided rulings (`R<n>`), the owner's laws in the mockup's `WIRING.md`, and the roadmap passages the register rows cite, as repository paths.
- **Permission keys** are listed once in the Permission key catalogue below; tickets cite it.
- **Who may do it (SP-9, 27 September).** An actor word in a row or in the register ("agency member", "agency owner/admin", "administrator", "permissioned person") names an install-default grant bundle, never a role the software checks: every write is checked against a grant row (scope, collection, action; `research/minimum-contract-2026-09-10/CONTRACT.md` 3.2). Each build ticket names the permission key per command (for example `task:write`, `task:share`, `report:share`, `custody:manage`, `billing:manage`) and whether an agent may hold it. "Anyone signed in" is for shell navigation only.
- **Built on** (section 19): where a decided tool already does a capability's job, the capability wraps it and the row says so; "owned" means the product builds it.
- **Precedence (27 September, lane SPEC-REVIEW-FOLD).** Where a capability row here, a register row in `PLACEHOLDERS.md` or a ruling in `CATALOGUE.md` differs from an acceptance line in `docs/mockup-inventory/TICKET-PLAN.md` or `TICKET-DRAFTS.md`, the row or ruling wins: the ticket plan fixes the look and the mockup address, and each build ticket's behaviour is written from its capability rows. The ticket plan's rulings all have outcomes (TICKET-PLAN section 2).
- The timer is decided (the owner, 27 September): it is built in the Tasks phase, outside the first-slice (T1) demo.

## Permission key catalogue

Lane GRILL-FOLD, 27 September 2026, on the scoping decision "one key catalogue before the first phase 2 ticket" (FU-1-KEYS, decided, veto open). Every key a build ticket's Permissions table names is here, gathered from the ticket drafts' proposals plus the wayfinder keys (research note W12, `research/wayfinder-scoping-2026-09-27/W12.md`). Tickets cite this table; a builder who needs a key not listed adds it here first. Keys are `collection:action` on the grant model (minimum contract 3.1: read, comment, write, assign, decide, share, manage).

- **Install defaults.** An agency member holds read, comment, write and assign on the collections and clients they are granted; the owner and administrators hold every action; nobody else holds decide, share or manage by default. An installation can narrow any of these. On a map, its creator is its owner and holds `task:decide` and `task:manage` on it.
- **Agents.** An agent, in the app or at the CLI (CS-15.18), holds only what its delegation narrows from a person's grants and never decide, share or manage (contract 2.3 to 2.6; TR-A-5). System writes run under a worker lease, not a grant.
- **Token-bound acts** (lane PI-FOLD-1, TR-S-PI2-12): accepting an invitation (C39-T, C39-C) and setting a password from a reset link (C40) happen before the person can sign in, so no grant can authorise them. Their authority is a one-time token: unspent, unexpired, bound to its invitation or reset request, its address and its business, and never logged. The login an accepted invitation creates is a system write under that token, as the effect of the inviter's `access:share` act.
- **The step-up set: money actions only** (the owner, 28 September 2026, owner lines 38 and 40): every `billing` key, `offer:decide`, `mandate:manage` and `spend:decide` (billing, invoices and Xero drafts, payment links, ad spend and budgets, accepting a priced offer or quote). A command holding one needs the second factor within the last 60 minutes (a client, who may have none, signs in afresh), checked once inside the grant check (C59), while the installation's money step-up setting is on; it is on by default, only the owner or an administrator can switch it off, and each switch is audited. Releasing to a client, publishing, sending to an audience, gate approvals, and share and manage actions need no re-check: that scope, every `share`, `manage` and `decide` key with a 15-minute window (lanes TR-FOLD2 and TR-FOLD3), is dropped on the owner's ruling. A token refresh never renews the window (TR-SEC4-6).
- **Two type rules on the task collection** (owner, #602): a grilling or prototype ticket resolves, and a map's ticket batch is accepted, only by the map's owner, a person. A grant scoped to a map record covers the map and its subtasks; no wayfinder collection exists. A ticket's type changes to or from grilling, prototype or map only by the map's owner (`task:decide`); an agent's retype of such a ticket is refused, so a type change cannot route around these rules (final plan review, lane FINAL-FOLD; WF-1, WF-2).

| `task:share` | owner and administrators | no | MP-4-8 | change a task's client (`task.set_party`; DP-19 "share authority"). A task's client can be changed only while the task is empty: its history holds nothing beyond its creation and earlier client changes, so no comment, file, doc, time entry, link, approval or other change. The change is one step, through `task.set_party`, on every path (the app, the API and the command line), by a person holding `task:share`; an agent is refused. Once the task has content its client is locked, with no move and no unlock on any path: `task.set_party` refuses with `CLIENT_LOCKED` (409) and writes nothing (`S0-5 client change refused once the task has content`, `MP-4-8 locked task refuses a client change`). To serve another client, "Duplicate without contents" (`task.duplicate`) makes a new task for the chosen client from the bare shell only (title, type, and the names of its checklist items and subtasks), which the person sees and can edit first; the old task is untouched, and the new task's business-internal history records "duplicated from" the old task's id (`MP-4-8 duplicate carries only the shell`, `MP-4-8 duplicate gives no way back to the old task`). This is the owner's design of 28 September 2026 (owner line 75), which replaced the closed-world move. Carrying the title and the item and subtask names is the owner's ruling; the duplicate form marks each carried free-text field, warns when the old client's name or a recorded alias is in it, and the person confirms the carried text before creating (`MP-4-8 carried text warns on the old client's name`). The duplicate needs current read on the old task and `task:write` for the chosen client, both checked in the command, and is person-only: an agent credential is refused even with delegated `task:write`. "Duplicated from" shows the old task's id only to a reader with current read on it (lane PIR7-FIX). |

## Build order: phase first, then slice

Inside a phase, the build units' dependency-based wave schedule (`docs/build-units.md`) supersedes numerical slice order: a slice's units run in the wave their dependencies allow (lane TR-FOLD, 28 September 2026, TR-A-13).

Lane SPEC-REVIEW-FOLD, 27 September 2026 (`evidence/SPEC-REVIEW.md`, SO-2). This is the one build order. It follows conflict X6 (section 18): the roadmap's eight-phase order stands, and a ticket-plan slice is built in the phase that supplies its data and authority, split where it spans phases (`evidence/SLICE-INVENTORY.md` section 2.1). It replaces the ticket plan's own order (`TICKET-PLAN.md` section 1). Lane ALIGN-FOLD (27 September) brought the table into line with the build units' recorded splits and moves: MP-9-1 to phase 2, MP-7-12 to phase 7, MP-10-5 to phase 8, MP-12-5 split into 5a (phase 6) and 5b (phase 8), MP-13-15 split into its six tabs; the Bookmarks panel (MP-7-4) and the scratch pad (MP-7-5) are deferred with no ticket (roadmap#121). Lane LEARN-CHAT (27 September) added C71 to phase 2 and C72 to phase 3. A ticket depends only on tickets in its own phase or an earlier one; within a phase, slices go in number order, except that slice 13 comes before slice 10, whose reports carry its source chips.

| CS-4.12 | Change the task's client while it is empty; duplicate it without contents once it is locked. A task's client can be changed only while the task is empty: its history holds nothing beyond its creation and earlier client changes, so no comment, file, doc, time entry, link, approval or other change. The change is one step, through `task.set_party`, on every path (the app, the API and the command line), by a person holding `task:share`; an agent is refused. Once the task has content its client is locked, with no move and no unlock on any path: `task.set_party` refuses with `CLIENT_LOCKED` (409) and writes nothing (`S0-5 client change refused once the task has content`, `MP-4-8 locked task refuses a client change`). To serve another client, "Duplicate without contents" (`task.duplicate`) makes a new task for the chosen client from the bare shell only (title, type, and the names of its checklist items and subtasks), which the person sees and can edit first; the old task is untouched, and the new task's business-internal history records "duplicated from" the old task's id (`MP-4-8 duplicate carries only the shell`, `MP-4-8 duplicate gives no way back to the old task`). This is the owner's design of 28 September 2026 (owner line 75), which replaced the closed-world move. Carrying the title and the item and subtask names is the owner's ruling; the duplicate form marks each carried free-text field, warns when the old client's name or a recorded alias is in it, and the person confirms the carried text before creating (`MP-4-8 carried text warns on the old client's name`). The duplicate needs current read on the old task and `task:write` for the chosen client, both checked in the command, and is person-only: an agent credential is refused even with delegated `task:write`. "Duplicated from" shows the old task's id only to a reader with current read on it (lane PIR7-FIX). | `DP-19` | `FA-TASKS-54` | `task.client changed`; `task duplicated` · audited | MP-4-8 Dock task panel | research/fixed-slots-2026-09-10/CONTRACT.md:293 |

| CS-13.31 | C26 A/B experiment records, in the build: for ads A/B tests and conversion-rate optimisation (ad copy, landing pages, forms and offers), record a test (hypothesis, variants, dates, minimum days), show live results and confidence, and record the outcome, which becomes a prior on recommendations; the Testing tab appears once an experiment record exists. Arms are read, not re-run: Google Ads and Meta arms from the metrics their connections already sync (their APIs give per-arm metrics, not a verdict), page, form and offer variants from GA4 sessions and enquiries by variant (Ops Astro forms record the variant), or a client's connected testing tool. One scoring method for every test: Bayesian chance to beat control with a prior Normal(0, 0.3) on the relative lift and a 95% credible interval (GrowthBook's published method), shown as 'confidence' against the 95% call threshold. It shows 'too early to call' until the minimum days pass. ## 15a. The agent interface and the wayfinder mapping

Lane GRILL-FOLD, 27 September 2026, on the owner's requirements A and B and the two addenda of the live grilling (map #396). Plan only.

**Where it already stood.** The agent interface is not new: one access path for app, portal, API and CLI, with no privileged surface and a three-way parity test, was decided on 10 September (#46; `docs/deep-modules-proposal.md`, "One access path"; `docs/decisions/build-and-review.md`, "Surfaces": "agents should be able to complete and update tasks through the CLI from the beginning"), and the first slice already carries it (the HTTP boundary T1f3 and the parity tests T1g1 and T1g2 in `docs/build-plan.md`). The MCP face was deferred until asked for (`sources/research-snapshots/synthesis/plan-v2.md`, the MCP line). What the owner added: parity for every UI action as the build grows, the wayfinder operations and the tracker backend on it from phase 2 (C69, C70), and the lightweight, right-sized rules below. Nothing recorded puts the API later, so there is no conflict.

**Build tickets** (build map drafts, lane GRILL-FOLD): API-1 the command catalogue and parity check; API-2 the agent credential; API-3 the CLI; API-4 the context bundles, read models and changes-since reads; API-5 the tracker backend; WF-1 to WF-13 for wayfinder. The budget below is in the acceptance checks of API-3 to API-5.

**The budget (CS-15.19).** Targets for waste, never caps on correctness; the completeness check wins any tie. Tokens are counted by a local tokenizer fixed in the test suite (no paid call), over a seeded fixture map of 40 tickets with realistic threads.

| Measure | Target | How it is checked |
|---|---|---|
| A write's result (create, update, link, comment, resolve), default output | under 150 tokens | every write command in the fixture, largest result |
| A brief read (get or one list page of 20) | under 300 tokens | every read command at brief |
| A standard read of one task | under 800 tokens | every task in the fixture, 95th percentile |
| *Map status* (frontier, fog, counts) | one call; under 1,000 tokens for the 40-ticket map | one request logged per call |
| *Work this ticket* | one call; under 3,000 tokens at standard, with full text of any linked document on request | one request logged per call |
| Completeness | a lane working a fixture ticket from its bundle alone makes no follow-up read for anything the ticket depends on | a scripted agent run per ticket type, zero follow-up reads recorded |
| What changed since | returns only records changed after the point, in one call | a fixture edit, then the read, compared |
| The CLI's whole help, as an agent loads it | under 1,500 tokens | measured on the built help text |
| Round trips | one per call; a bundle is one query on its read model | query count per call, recorded by the test |
| Services | none added | the installation's service list is unchanged |

**The one mapping table** (requirement A; research W16). The upstream skills stay unmodified; when they change, this table is the one place updated, and the conformance run (C70) checks both backends.

| Skill concept (the wayfinder and grilling skills) | GitHub | Ops Astro |
|---|---|---|
| Map | an issue labelled `wayfinder:map` | a task of type "map" (CS-15.6) |
| Ticket | a sub-issue of the map | a subtask of the map (CS-15.7) |
| Ticket type: research, prototype, grilling, task | label `wayfinder:<type>` | the task's type field; plus "build" for build tickets |
| Destination, Notes | sections of the map issue body | the map's Destination and Notes components |
| Decisions so far | lines appended to the map body, one per closed ticket, linking it | rendered from resolved subtasks with their gist; `map revised (decision added)` |
| Not yet specified (fog) | a section of the map body | patch items with ids; `fog graduated (patch, tickets)` |
| Out of scope | a section of the map body | Out of scope items, linking closed tickets |
| Blocking | native "blocked by" dependency | the task "blocked by" link |
| Frontier | open, unblocked, unassigned children, by query | the frontier read model; *map status* in one call |
| Claim | assign the issue, first | `ticket claimed` (assignment), first |
| Resolution | resolution comment, close, pointer on the map | `ticket resolved (answer, gist)` on the thread, close, the rendered line |
| Grilling session | the conversation, the answer posted on the ticket | the grilling component: the exchange recorded on the grilling ticket |
| Research artifact | a file on a `research/<name>` branch, linked | a Docs page linked to the ticket (CS-15.7); from phase 4 (WF-8), the tracker backend answering "not available until Docs" before then (final plan review) |
| Rule out of scope | close the ticket, one line in Out of scope | close as out of scope (`task:decide`), one Out of scope item |
| Tracker operations file | `issue-tracker-github.md` | `issue-tracker-ops-astro.md`, over the C69 CLI (CS-15.20) |

## 16a. Out of scope and deferred

The owner, 27 September 2026, on the new candidates (verbatim): *"not worried about doing email templates the whole email thing that not not really worried about don't even know what booking defaults are"*. These two capabilities are out of scope for now, and C27 joined them the same day (the owner, reviewing the list: *"yeah we'll get rid of the local grid then"*): no ticket goes to the build map and their reserved Settings tabs stay unbuilt. This lane reads "the whole email thing" as the whole of C29, the template administration: the batched client-mention email the owner decided for version one (C33-2, `docs/decisions/delivery-and-presence.md`) keeps fixed wording and is not taken out by it. Settled on 27 September with the list review: C29 means the email-template screen only, and the version-one batched client-mention email stays (Owner answers, the note under the list).

**Also out of scope** (owner answer 21, 27 September): the Hub's old journey engine (stall nudges, welcome flows, speed-to-lead, the five lifecycle pipelines) retires beside the email templates; the journey-stage field, the five-day chase and event-triggered automations stay. It has no capability row, so no count changes.

**Deferred** is not out of scope: the capability stays the direction and gets no ticket now. Two items are deferred: C37 web push (its row said "later, not version one"; moved here by lane SPEC-REVIEW-FOLD) and C13 (the owner, reviewing the list: *"the brief read aloud the whole idea is that we just have kokoro and then eventually we'll just be able to have it so then you can read or chat in any format that you like you can even chat with like the agents and just have it set up that way but we're not gonna worry about that for now"*).

## 18. Conflicts: how each was settled

Every conflict that reached this lane: the five that stood in `PLACEHOLDERS.md` (PH-1 to PH-5), the fourteen contradictions in `evidence/SLICE-INVENTORY.md` section 3.2 (X1 to X14), the two the cross-check left for the owner in `ASTRA-CROSSCHECK.md` (DR-64, DR-65), and the fresh audit's flags (47). The rule applied: where the mockup and the roadmap disagree and the mockup's behaviour is not a law in the owner's own words, the roadmap wins (`DIRECTION.md` point 7); where two of the owner's own rulings disagree, the later one wins; where a draft contract disagrees with a decided ruling, the ruling wins; where nothing decides and one reading is obvious, it is decided and recorded. What remained was a real conflict between the owner's words and the roadmap, or two sensible readings that lead to different builds. The owner answered every one on 27 September (the last section).

| Conflict | What | Outcome | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| PH-1 | Client access: share grant (R45) or `client_visible` (draft contract) | settled | R45 is decided and the draft contract (`research/fixed-slots-2026-09-10/CONTRACT.md:310`) yields to it; one operation writes the grant and the field together. |
| PH-2 | Roll back to snapshot | settled | R78 (the owner) keeps it drawn unavailable; when the executor can reverse, it raises a gated reversal request with a receipt (`docs/decisions/execution.md`, effect reversibility), so no in-place undo is offered (AW-08, product issue 33). |
| PH-3 | Reject on the gate | settled | `docs/decisions/execution.md:49`: Request changes is bounded to two rounds, then approve, reject or escalate; the first slice draws two controls (`research/task-demo-spec-2026-09-11/SPEC.md:708`). Reject and Escalate appear at the bound, in the gate box. |
| PH-4 | A client taking back an approval | answered: owner answer 3 | Two sensible readings: the register allows only a comment after Approve; the fresh pass lets Request changes supersede an approval until publish. |
| PH-5 | Which decisions need four eyes | settled | The owner's ruling (money over a per-business threshold, `research/conversations/addendum-2026-09-14-12.md:114`, `docs/build-plan.md:187`) wins over the draft contract's gate rule (`research/minimum-contract-2026-09-10/CONTRACT.md:330`). |

## Owner answers

Answered by the owner, 27 September 2026 (relayed; lane ANSWERS24, `evidence/OWNER-ANSWERS.md`). Twenty-four items stood here, one line each with a recommendation: items 10 to 12 from the list review (`evidence/NEW-CAPABILITIES.md`), items 13 to 24 from the research and security lanes (`evidence/AUDIT-RECONCILE.md`). The owner took eighteen as recommended and answered six in their own terms (4, 12, 14, 15, 18, 19). Each answer is written into the rows it held, and no row waits on this list.

1. **Dashboard home.** As recommended: R1 (a), Portfolio Command at `/dashboard/`; an overview is added later only if the need shows. (AGENCY F1, R1; CS-14.30)
2. **Who signs off client cards.** As recommended: Approve and Request changes stay on every portal card; where a client's sign-off setting is off, the press is recorded as their response feeding the agency's decision; where it is on, it is the binding decision. (PORTAL F2, X13, R22; CS-11.15)
3. **A client changing their mind after Approve.** As recommended: Request changes stays live until publish and supersedes the approval as a new recorded decision, never an edit of it; after publish, a change is a new request. (PH-4; CS-11.15)
4. **Where client files live.** Answered, firmer than the recommendation: the client's Drive is home for the vast majority, if not all, production files, mirrored read-only (new candidate C63); Ops Astro storage holds what the product versions and approves; every client-facing file is served through the app under the client's grant. R68 becomes a real Drive listing once the mirror exists. (CLIENT FLAG-3, R68, RS-VAULT-3, SP-5; CS-12.1, CS-12.3, CS-12.10, CS-12.12, CS-16.13)
5. **Billing source.** As recommended: invoices and statements read from Xero through the installation's Xero connector (read, plus create drafts only); Pay now hands to Xero's own payment link; `payment started` and `payment settled` are recorded; no card data is held. (CLIENT FLAG-4, C16, R64; CS-12.14, CS-12.15, CS-12.24)
6. **A client ticket is a whole project.** As recommended: a ticket creates a task under a standing "Requests" project for that client, and staff promote it to its own project when it grows into work. (PORTAL F5, R28; CS-11.24)
7. **Model choice per conversation.** As recommended: the picker stays, offering only the models the client's model-egress setting allows, with the exact model id recorded on every run. (X9, DOCK C-5; CS-7.30)
8. **Dock seating order.** As recommended: float at the width asked for; `WIRING.md` §34.4 is amended by a note in `SIDEBAR.md` (the mockup repository is read-only). (DR-64; SIDEBAR T-D19)
9. **Small status text in the light theme.** As recommended: darker light-theme text variants for small status text; the current colours stay for lines, rules and icons. (DR-65; `TOKENS.md` DS-TOK-21 to DS-TOK-24)
10. **Email about a decision.** As recommended: decisions and incidents email at once, one email per item; everything else goes in the daily batch. (CS-2.17, CS-16.9)
11. **New client onboarding in the phase order.** As recommended: the agency's half right after Agent work; the client's half with the Client portal phase. (C41; CS-15.2 to CS-15.4)
12. **Wayfinder: ticket to build.** Answered: wayfinder inside Ops Astro mimics the whole GitHub interaction: tickets with comment threads; docs and comments synced into the back end and kept together; ticket types split as wayfinder splits them (prototype, research, grilling, task); a review section for spec tickets; adversarial review rounds scaled to the scope, by a reviewer from a different model family than the builder (the reviewer model is installation configuration); and gates, so nothing reaches production until its verifications, tests and prototypes pass. The automatic flow-on (map, spec, tickets, build) runs through those gates, with one acceptance of the tickets by the map's owner before building. (C42, C43, new C64 and C65; CS-15.7, CS-15.10, CS-15.14 to CS-15.16; `docs/roadmap.md`)
13. **Graduation and pre-approval sentences.** As recommended: a structured standing mandate (action classes and client picked from lists, a value ceiling, an expiry, revocable), checked by the system at every effect, with the sentence as its label only. (RA-6, SP-11; CS-14.17 to CS-14.19)
14. **Airbyte.** Answered: Airbyte carries the marketing data, and MainWP, Microsoft Clarity and the uptime monitor through custom Connector Builder sources; all three already run in one installation and are ported as installation-neutral definitions, so none is a build candidate (`evidence/OWNER-ANSWERS.md`, "Connector search"); inside the credential broker; the Connections rows read Airbyte's job history. Core Web Vitals keep the decided CrUX feed. (RA-15; CS-13.10, CS-13.12, CS-13.14, CS-13.15, CS-14.11, CS-14.27)
15. **Bookings.** Answered: Cal.com, behind the one booking card, fixed per installation; Ops Astro records booked, rescheduled and cancelled from Cal.com's signed events and never computes slots itself. (RA-26, RS-VAULT-8; CS-10.5 to CS-10.7, CS-10.16, CS-10.30)
16. **How a client's shape gets changed.** As recommended: one path, where an admin or the agent drafts a change as a plan and a person with the manager grant approves it in the app; no free-form field editor in the first CRM slice. (RC-17; C49, CS-2.24)
17. **A client's customers' enquiries.** As recommended: enquiries stay as the client's Workbench rows with an outcome and never enter the agency's People; a person is created only if the agency itself works with them. (RC-18; CS-10.23)
18. **Xero drafts.** Answered: no separate invoicing app sits in this path; billable time goes straight to Xero as a draft through the installation's Xero connector, which alone holds the token. **Decided 27 September:** Xero's free developer plan; no paid plan. (RS-VAULT-1, RA-27; C38, CS-12.28 to CS-12.30)
19. **SEMrush.** Answered: optional per installation, as configuration, with units from the installation's own SEMrush plan (set by each installation). It supersedes the ruling of 6 August 2026. (RS-VAULT-12; CS-13.27)
20. **Client email cap.** As recommended: the weekly cap for client relationship mail, enforced in the send path, with transactional mail outside it; the daily batch stays for staff. (RS-VAULT-6; CS-16.9)
21. **The old journey engine.** As recommended: retired, out of scope beside the email templates; the journey-stage field, the five-day chase and event-triggered automations stay. (RS-REPO-10, RS-VAULT-10; section 16a)
22. **Counts for client logins.** As recommended: for client logins, other clients' rows are absent, never counted. (SP-2; `PLACEHOLDERS.md` `B-22`)
23. **When the legal basics are due.** As recommended: the privacy policy, the notice for indirect collection and the client data-handling statement are ready before the first real client data and the first client invite. (SP-27)
24. **The Privacy Act.** As recommended: every client's personal information is treated as covered, and the data-handling statement says so. (SECURITY-PRIVACY section 6, item 3) **Added 27 September 2026 (package 2):** client content sent to a model goes to an overseas provider (at the start, the owner's own Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions), so the privacy policy lists it as an overseas disclosure, and the per-client model-egress setting (C60) still applies. Client folders in the agency's master Drive are shared with clients by public link, so anyone holding a link can open that folder (`docs/build-safeguards.md`, the overseas-services register).
